newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar sets 42-month high in Tokyo trade.
newsitem.headline: Dollar sets 42-month high in Tokyo trade.

text.p: The dollar rose to its highest level against the yen in 3-1/2 years on Monday, vaulting over a key psychological barrier at 113.60 yen in Asian trading.

Dealers said buying from Japanese investors and interbank traders propelled the greenback to 113.70 yen in Tokyo morning trade, its highest level since April 1993, in a continuing comeback from historic depths plumbed last year.
This compared with a rate of around 113.40 yen in late New York trade on Friday.

The 113.60 yen level had become a strong psychological barrier, or resistance point, in the market as it was close to the level at which then U.S. treasury secretary Lloyd Bentsen voiced concern over the depreciation of the yen in early January 1994.

The dollar slumped to a post-war global low of 79.75 yen in April 1995 but has gradually regained ground against the Japanese currency, helped by rounds of central bank intervention and Japanese steps to encourage capital to flow overseas into dollar-based instruments.

The dollar's rise has been fuelled by a prolonged period of low interest rates in Japan, which has encouraged Japanese investors to sell the yen in favour of higher yielding currencies like the dollar.
The dollar stood at around 113.65 yen in mid-morning trade.
